A malicious feed could supply a URL containing `'` characters to break out of the `href` attribute and inject arbitrary HTML/JS into the stored post, which is then served as `raw_html` bypassing the cooking pipeline. 3. **Bug (medium):** `topic_embed.rb:58-59` — `absolutize_urls` uses `uri.port` unconditionally. For a standard `http://` URL, `uri.port` returns `80` (the default), so the condition `uri.port != 80` saves it, but for a URL where the port is `nil` (malformed URIs that still pass the `https?://` regex check), this will raise `NoMethodError` on `nil.!=`. Actually on point 3 — `URI()` on a valid http/https URL always sets a default port, so nil is not possible there.
